superseded_open_pdks_commits.reason: volare-era pin; every record under sim/ and layout/ was minted against it
superseded_open_pdks_commits.remove_when: phase 2 (#670) repoints the records at the current pin

notes: Provenance: schema ported from 2AMLogic/sky130-bandgap's sim/pdk.json
(commit 1f04e8524cc2d8c2c7154773749b1b2d3be2ce64), per CLAUDE.md's
'Harness bootstrap' instruction, and adapted for this repo's harness
(sim/harness/*.py) instead of that repo's sim/bin/corner-run.py.
This file is the reproducibility pin for every record under sim/.
open_pdks_commit is the open_pdks revision of the sky130 PDK family,
installed with ciel (fleet re-pin, 2AMLogic/sky130-sar-adc#669); the
previous pin, c6d73a3, was installed with volare and is listed in
superseded_open_pdks_commits below. DR-001
(spec/decision-records/DR-001-supply-flavor-scope.md) enumerated the
installed device menu against that earlier pin. The harness reads the
SOURCES file at the root of $PDK_ROOT/$PDK (falling back to the version
hash volare encodes in the resolved path) and refuses to run against a
different revision unless --allow-toolchain-drift is passed (in which
case the record carries the mismatch). The search root is $PDK_ROOT,
else default_pdk_root, else each of fallback_pdk_roots in order -- so a
leftover ~/.volare is only found when ~/.ciel has no variant, and is
then reported as a mismatch rather than used silently.
superseded_open_pdks_commits lists pins that existing records are still
allowed to carry (sim/check_spec_coverage.py's pdk-pin-drift gate). Each
entry names the issue that added it and when to remove it; an entry
never makes the harness accept an install at that commit.
process_corners are the basic N/P device sections that actually exist in
the PDK ngspice library (verified against the '.lib' sections of
libs.tech/combined/sky130.lib.spice: tt, sf, ff, ss, fs, ll, hh, hl, lh,
then every one of those again with a _mm suffix). tt/ss/ff/sf/fs are the
standard MOS/BJT corners this repo's PVT runner uses by default -- they
also gate PNP Is/Bf/Nf via the same corners/<name>/nonfet.spice includes.
ll/hh/hl/lh (resistor/capacitor-only skew corners) exist and remain
available to experiment manifests that need them (a future CDAC unit-cap
characterization is the likely first user, per DR-001 Consequence #1) but
are not added to process_corners until a manifest actually uses one.
mismatch_corners are the '_mm' local-mismatch switch: they differ from
the plain corners only in setting MC_MM_SWITCH=1, which enables the
per-instance AGAUSS() terms inside the device subcircuits (the plain
'mc' sections instead set MC_PR_SWITCH=1, for global process Monte
Carlo -- not used by this harness). sim/monte_carlo.py drives ngspice at
a mismatch corner directly (varying only rndseed across draws), the same
way sky130-bandgap's sim/pnp-mismatch/ does, rather than going through
the PVT corner-matrix runner -- Monte Carlo sampling is not a corner
axis, so sim/harness/corners.py deliberately keeps it out of the plain
process_corners list.
